items.finding: In one in-line FTIR study, temperature was deliberately varied, alongside concentration and ionic strength, when building the calibration model so that the model would be robust.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that for the customer's petroleum stream, process temperature at the measurement point should be recorded and deliberately included as a variation in the first comparison experiment, so the calibration can cover the real operating envelope. A process temperature sensor at the measurement point would provide this input.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source concerns aqueous acid systems in lithium recycling, not petroleum, and temperature variation there served model robustness rather than a separate auxiliary sensor requirement. Transfer to hydrocarbon matrices and to the customer's temperature range is untested.

citation.quote: The concentrations of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid as well as the ionic strength and temperature were varied to obtain a robust model.
